Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal at Acme reviewed the MSA + Order Form and attached a tracked-redlines doc (ACME_Redlines_20260530.docx) with four principal asks that need clarification before procurement can move forward: 

1) Output ownership: They want explicit language that gives Acme ownership (or a perpetual, transferable license) of customer-generated outputs and derivative models created from those outputs.
2) Training/data use: They request an opt-in for model training (no training by default) and proof that telemetry used for improvements is de-identified.
3) Feedback license: They want any feedback Acme provides to be limited to product improvements and not used to train a model that will be commercialized without consent.
4) Telemetry & audit: They need a list of telemetry fields retained, retention periods, and whether logs are exportable for their audit team.

We flagged a handful of redlines in the doc where the Order Form references "Customer Content" and "Productized Outputs." Please review the attached and let me know the quickest path to resolve — our procurement window is tight; they'd like a commercial/legal response by end of day Tuesday (PST).

If it'd help, Jing can join a 30-min call with your legal team to walk the redlines.

Thanks,
Sam

Sam, Mina — quick commercial note from our side before Laura jumps into legal language: we want to offer clear options to speed procurement. Two pragmatic paths that reflect common market practice: 

Option A (Enterprise friendly, higher commitment): Acme receives a perpetual, non-exclusive, transferable license to Outputs and Derivatives for the specific Product(s) licensed via the Order Form. Redwood retains the right to use aggregated telemetry for product improvements; training on Acme data requires Acme opt-in. Pricing: +15% list to cover model isolation/ops.

Option B (Lower price, more constraints): Acme receives a time-limited license to Outputs for internal use only (e.g., 5-year term), no transferability to third parties, and an explicit ban on commercializing derivatives without Redwood consent. Training on customer data is opt-in; telemetry export & auditability included. Pricing: standard list.

If you prefer we can mark the Order Form with Option A/B and Laura can add the exact language. To address telemetry: we can provide a table of fields and retention — Mina, can ops produce that by EOD Monday?

If quick + decision-oriented, we can accept a Monday AM sync and aim to have a draft back to you by COB Tuesday.

Thanks,

Hi Sam / Jing — Laura from Legal here. Thanks for the clear redlines. A few specific points and proposed redline language so your counsel can see concrete text: 

1) Output/Derivative language (Order Form §2.1): propose replacing "Customer may use Outputs" with: "Customer is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to Outputs, and a perpetual, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to Derivatives for internal use, unless a separate written agreement grants transfer rights." This keeps productization flexibility for Redwood while giving Acme a durable right to use Outputs.

2) Training/Data Use (MSA §5.3): we will accept default = no training without opt-in. Draft: "Redwood will not train models on Customer Content or Outputs without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood may use de‑identified, aggregated telemetry for service improvement; telemetry schemas will be provided."

3) Feedback license: propose narrow carve — "Customer feedback provided via official channels is licensed to Redwood on a non-exclusive, perpetual basis for product improvement only; such Feedback will not be used to create Customer‑specific commercial models without an additional agreement."

4) Telemetry & auditability: we will provide a telemetry-field export and retention table; however, we cannot commit to indefinite retention. Proposed retention windows will be included in the export. Please confirm Acme's required retention for audit purposes.

If Acme confirms transferability and a 365-day retention window, commercial will need to move to Option A pricing. If transferability is not required and retention is 90 days, Option B is feasible. Happy to hop on a call; if not, we will produce a redline document and pricing sheet by COB Tuesday.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
